@@ -167,20 +167,7 @@ struct SwitcherRailView: View {

       .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Self.cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
-      // The drop shadow, cast by a plain shape BEHIND the glass and mounted AFTER the clip.
-      //
-      // Three things had to be true here, each found by looking at the screen rather than reasoning:
-      // the window cannot cast it (a borderless non-opaque panel produces no system shadow at all —
-      // measured, zero darkening at any distance, with glass content and with a solid fill); a clip
-      // applies to a view's background, so a shadow mounted alongside the glass was clipped away
-      // entirely; and a layer shadow on the representable didn't render either. A SwiftUI shape's shadow
-      // does. The fill is the theme's own card colour, so on the chance the glass lets any of it through
-      // it reads as the rail's surface rather than a dark slab.
-      .background {
-        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Self.cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
-          .fill(theme.tokens.panel)
-          .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.30), radius: 14, y: 5)
-      }
+      .background { shadowCaster }

+  /// The rail's drop shadow: the shape's shadow with **the shape itself punched out**, mounted behind the
+  /// glass and after the clip.
+  ///
+  /// Every part of that is load-bearing, and each was measured rather than reasoned:
+  ///
+  /// - **The window can't cast it.** A borderless, non-opaque `NSPanel` produces no system shadow at all —
+  ///   `hasShadow = true` with `invalidateShadow()` darkened nothing at 6/14/26/44pt out on any side, with

+  /// - **A clip applies to a view's background**, so a shadow mounted alongside the glass was clipped away
+  ///   entirely. Hence a second `.background`, after `.clipShape`.
+  /// - **A layer shadow on the representable never rendered**, `shadowPath` and all. A SwiftUI shape's
+  ///   shadow does.
+  /// - **The hole is what keeps the glass alive.** A shadow needs an opaque caster, and an opaque layer

+          .compositingGroup()
+      }
+  }

2	import SwiftUI

4	/// One rail card's data — a **value type**, resolved once when the rail opens.
5	///
6	/// INVARIANT (prior learning `macapp-row-observes-sessions-invalidation-storm`): no rail view may hold
7	/// an `AppStore` or `TerminalSessions`. `TerminalSessions` republishes on every title/activity pulse,
8	/// so a card observing it to decide "am I the cursor" would re-render at OSC frequency — the
9	/// WORKROOM-2B hang. Everything a card draws is snapshotted here instead.
10	struct SwitcherCard: Identifiable, Equatable {
11	  /// What the well draws. The two switchers have genuinely different identity problems, so they get
12	  /// genuinely different wells: workrooms differ from each other by *which workroom they are*, panes
13	  /// inside one workroom differ by *what kind of thing they are*.
14	  enum Well: Equatable {
15	    /// ⌥Tab: a stable colour + monogram you learn, the way you learn an app icon.
16	    case mark(SwitcherMark)
17	    /// ⌃Tab: a small graphic drawn from the pane's own data, so the shape says the kind.
18	    case miniature(PaneMiniature)
19	  }
20	
21	  let id: String
22	  /// The primary line. Already prefix-stripped by `WorkroomLabel.railTitles` where applicable.
23	  let title: String
24	  /// The stable identity zone of the subtitle — never empty, never churns.
25	  let stableSubtitle: String
26	  /// The live tail (a command line, a diffstat). Truncates before `stableSubtitle` does.
27	  let liveSubtitle: String?
28	  var well: Well
29	  let badge: Int
30	  let isRunning: Bool
31	
32	  var subtitle: String {
33	    guard let liveSubtitle, !liveSubtitle.isEmpty else { return stableSubtitle }
34	    return "\(stableSubtitle) · \(liveSubtitle)"
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	extension SwitcherCard {
39	  /// Build the rail's cards, with mark hues rotated so no two visible marks share a colour.
40	  @MainActor
41	  static func cards(for items: [QuickSwitcherController.Item]) -> [SwitcherCard] {
42	    var cards = items.map(SwitcherCard.init(item:))
43	    // Only workroom cards carry marks; pane miniatures are unaffected.
44	    let markIndices = cards.indices.filter {
45	      if case .mark = cards[$0].well { true } else { false }
46	    }
47	    let hues = markIndices.map { index -> Int in
48	      guard case .mark(let mark) = cards[index].well else { return 0 }
49	      return mark.hue
50	    }
51	    for (position, index) in zip(SwitcherMark.disambiguate(hues), markIndices) {
52	      guard case .mark(let mark) = cards[index].well else { continue }
53	      cards[index].well = .mark(SwitcherMark(monogram: mark.monogram, hue: position))
54	    }
55	    return cards
56	  }
57	
58	  /// Snapshot a controller item into a card. Reads the stores ONCE, here, and never again — which is
59	  /// also why this is `@MainActor` while `SwitcherCard` itself is not: the reads happen on the main
60	  /// actor at reveal, and what the views then hold is inert.
61	  @MainActor
62	  init(item: QuickSwitcherController.Item) {
63	    switch item {
64	    case .workroom(let slot):
65	      let label = slot.store?.label(for: slot.sid)
66	      id = "wr:\(slot.target.id)"
67	      let displayed = label?.distinguishing ?? slot.target.title
68	      title = displayed
69	      // The monogram follows the DISPLAYED name so it matches what you read; the colour follows the
70	      // target id, which a relabel doesn't change — so relabelling re-letters the mark without moving
71	      // the hue you actually recognise.
72	      well = .mark(SwitcherMark(displayName: displayed, stableKey: slot.target.id))
73	      stableSubtitle = label?.branch ?? label?.project ?? ""
74	      liveSubtitle = slot.store.flatMap { Self.vcsTail(for: slot.sid, in: $0) }
75	      badge = slot.store?.notifications.count(target: slot.target.id) ?? 0
76	      isRunning = slot.store?.isRunCommandRunning(for: slot.target.id) ?? false
77	    case .pane(let tab):
78	      id = "pane:\(tab.id)"
79	      title = tab.title
80	      let miniature = PaneMiniature(content: tab.content, isRunning: tab.isRunning)
81	      well = .miniature(miniature)
82	      stableSubtitle = miniature.label
83	      liveSubtitle = nil
84	      badge = 0
85	      isRunning = tab.isRunning
86	    }
87	  }
88	
89	  /// A workroom's VCS state as the subtitle's live tail: line counts when known, otherwise the coarse
90	  /// state. Conflicts win — they are the one state you want to notice from a switcher.
91	  @MainActor
92	  static func vcsTail(for sid: SidebarID, in store: AppStore) -> String? {
93	    guard let status = store.workroomStatuses[sid] else { return nil }
94	    if status.conflicted { return "conflicts" }
95	    if let added = status.insertions, let removed = status.deletions, added + removed > 0 {
96	      return "+\(added) −\(removed)"
97	    }
98	    if status.dirty == true { return "modified" }
99	    if status.dirty == false { return "clean" }
100	    return nil
101	  }
102	}
103	
104	/// The rail's observable state. One object, mutated by `SwitcherPanelController` — the cards
105	/// themselves observe nothing.
106	@MainActor
107	final class SwitcherRailModel: ObservableObject {
108	  @Published var cards: [SwitcherCard] = []
109	  @Published var cursor = 0
110	  @Published var width: CGFloat = 600
111	  /// Bumped on a theme change so the tokens are re-read.
112	  @Published var themeVersion = 0
113	
114	  var onHover: ((Int) -> Void)?
115	  var onCommit: ((Int) -> Void)?
116	
117	  func update(cards: [SwitcherCard], cursor: Int, width: CGFloat) {
118	    self.cards = cards
119	    self.cursor = cursor
120	    self.width = width
121	  }
122	}

124	/// The rail: **one** row of label-led cards, centred in a floating translucent panel.
125	///
126	/// Label-led, and screenshot-free. Window captures were built and removed: at any size that fits a
127	/// switcher rail an aspect-fit terminal capture is a grey smudge, and it is neither stable nor
128	/// distinctive — it changes every time and every terminal looks like every other terminal. What
129	/// replaced it differs per switcher, because the two have different identity problems: a workroom is
130	/// distinguished by *which workroom it is* (so it gets a learnable mark), a pane inside one workroom by
131	/// *what kind of thing it is* (so it gets a drawn miniature of its type).
132	struct SwitcherRailView: View {
133	  @ObservedObject var model: SwitcherRailModel
134	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
135	
136	  /// Re-resolved per render. `model.themeVersion` is read in `body` so a theme change actually
137	  /// repaints — this is a static view inside a panel that is only ever ordered in and out, so nothing
138	  /// else would invalidate it.
139	  private var palette: SwitcherRailLayout.Palette { SwitcherRailLayout.palette(for: theme.tokens) }
140	
141	  /// No `accessibilityReduceMotion` here on purpose: nothing in the rail animates. The cursor ring and
142	  /// the scroll offset both snap (a 0.32s spring per step would still be travelling toward card 2 when
143	  /// the commit lands on card 4), and the panel itself carries `animationBehavior = .none`.
144	
145	  private var cardWidth: CGFloat {
146	    SwitcherRailLayout.cardWidth(count: model.cards.count, available: model.width)
147	  }
148	
149	  private var scrolls: Bool {
150	    SwitcherRailLayout.scrolls(count: model.cards.count, available: model.width)
151	  }
152	
153	  var body: some View {
154	    row
155	      .id(model.themeVersion)  // see `palette` — the only thing that invalidates this view
156	      // The system's Liquid Glass — the same surface ⌘Tab sits on — rather than the app's
157	      // `sidebarCard` recipe, whose `.withinWindow` material has nothing to sample inside a transparent
158	      // floating panel. No full-screen dim: a 250ms gesture must not flash the whole screen, so the
159	      // separation is the material itself.
160	      .background {
161	        ZStack {
162	          RailGlassBackground(cornerRadius: Self.cornerRadius)
163	          // D14's last resort: a theme whose foreground cannot clear the text floor against a
164	          // translucent surface gets an opaque one instead. Legibility outranks the material — and
165	          // without this the glass would keep washing text that already failed its contrast check.
166	          if palette.needsOpaqueFill { theme.tokens.panel }
167	        }
168	      }
169	      .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Self.cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
170	      .background { shadowCaster }
171	      // The halo the rail's drop shadow lands in. The window is `shadowMargin` bigger than the slab on
172	      // every side for exactly this — a drawn shadow is clipped at the window's edge, and the window
173	      // itself casts none (see `SwitcherRailLayout.shadowMargin`).
174	      .padding(SwitcherRailLayout.shadowMargin)
175	      .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
176	      .accessibilityIdentifier("switcher.rail")
177	  }
178

190	  ///   glass content and with a solid opaque fill alike.
191	  /// - **A clip applies to a view's background**, so a shadow mounted alongside the glass was clipped away
192	  ///   entirely. Hence a second `.background`, after `.clipShape`.
193	  /// - **A layer shadow on the representable never rendered**, `shadowPath` and all. A SwiftUI shape's
194	  ///   shadow does.
195	  /// - **The hole is what keeps the glass alive.** A shadow needs an opaque caster, and an opaque layer
196	  ///   anywhere beneath a glass view destroys the material completely: sampled across the rail's interior,
197	  ///   glass normally tracks its backdrop (correlation +0.81), and with an opaque fill behind it the

199	  ///   spill: `destinationOut` removes its own footprint, and the mask's rectangle is expanded by

215	  }

content.text:
This is a purely visual SwiftUI change: it replaces one `.background { RoundedRectangle().fill().shadow() }` view with a computed `shadowCaster` property that draws the same drop shadow, punching out the shape via a destinationOut mask so an opaque fill doesn't destroy the glass material behind it.

No entry points, no sinks, no data flow, no attacker-influenceable input. No shell/exec/SQL/FS/network/deserialization/auth/IPC/logging surface is touched. The change is scoped to a static view's rendering. Nothing to flag.
